textbookText: 6. Alimentary canal is straight and complete with mouth, pharynx, intestine and anus. 7. There are no circulatory and respiratory organs. Transport of materials occurs with the

help of pseudocoelomic fluid and respiration occurs through general body surface by diffusion in free living forms. Parasitic forms respire anaerobically. 8. Excretion occurs through a system of canals or tubes; renette cells and protonephridia in some cases. 9. Nervous system consists of ganglionated nerve rings around pharynx and a number of longitudinal nerve cords. 10. The sensory organs are in the form of papillae, eye spots, bristles and pits. 11. They are mostly unisexual with sexual dimorphism and having relatively simple reproductive organs. Males are usually smaller. 12. They do not reproduce asexually but sexual reproduction takes place by the fusion of sperms and ovum. 13. Fertilization is internal. Eggs are shelled and life cycle is either simple or complicated, usually with no larval forms.

Unique features Body is thread like, usually cylindrical in outline, pseudocoelomate, first animals with complete alimentary canal, excretion through renette cells (H-shaped excretory canal), distinct sexual dimorphism, No asexual reproduction Classification Phylym nemathelminthes is divided into two main classes based on the presence or absence of phasmids (caudal sense organs). Class1: Phasmida (Secernentea): i. This class consists of many parasitic forms. Free living forms largely inhabits soil. ii. They usually possess pore like amphids in the lateral lips. iii. There is the presence of paired phasmids in the caudal region. iv. Only anterior testis is found. v. There is well developed excretory system with renette cells. vi. Presence of glandular tail.
Example: Ascaris (round worm), Wuchereria (filarial worm), Loa loa (eye worm), Ancylostoma (hook worm) etc.

Class: 2 Aphasmida (Adenophorea) i. They are mostly free living found in water and soil. Some of them are parasitic. ii. Variously shaped amphids are found behind the lips. iii. There are no phasmids in the caudal area. iv. Paired testes are present. v. Excretory system is absent or reduced. vi. Presence of non-glandular tail.
Example: Mermis, Enoplus, Dorylaimus, Trichinella etc.
